prompt: Where does a Robolectric test's source file go?
hint: The same folder as plain JUnit.

choices.text: `app/src/test`
choices.why: Right: it runs on the JVM like a plain unit test.

choices.text: `app/src/androidTest`, with the device tests
choices.why: That folder is for tests that run on a device.

choices.text: `app/src/robolectric`, a folder of its own
choices.why: No such source set exists.

choices.text: `app/src/main`, beside the code it tests
choices.why: Test code never ships inside the app.

prompt: In section 02's timings, why did each Robolectric test take seconds when each `WeekTest` took almost nothing?
hint: What does a plain test never pay for?

choices.text: The JVM is slower for Compose code than for plain Kotlin
choices.why: The code runs at the same speed; the start-up is the cost.

choices.text: Robolectric tests are compiled again for every run
choices.why: Compilation is outside the test's recorded time.

choices.text: Most of it is starting the stand-in Android
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: They wait for a device before giving up
choices.why: They need no device at all.

prompt: A function computes the minutes left in a session from two `LocalTime` values. Where should its test run?
hint: Push each check as far left as it can go.

choices.text: Plain JUnit
choices.why: Right: it is only Kotlin and `java.time`.

choices.text: In a screenshot test of the session screen
choices.why: A picture cannot say which number is wrong.

choices.text: On an emulator, to use the phone's clock
choices.why: Nothing here needs the phone.

choices.text: Under Robolectric, because it is an Android app
choices.why: Being in an Android app does not make code use Android.

prompt: Where did section 03 read what each failed test expected and what it got?
hint: Gradle's summary only gave the line numbers.

choices.text: In the HTML report only, which needs a browser
choices.why: The same messages are in the XML results.

choices.text: In the Gradle summary line `3 tests completed`
choices.why: That line only counts.

choices.text: In the test's source code
choices.why: The source says what was expected, not what came back.

choices.text: In the result files, under each failure's message
choices.why: Right: the second command listed them.

prompt: With the mistake in place, how many minutes did the planned total come to, asked on that Sunday?
A colleague's test data has sessions only from Tuesday to Friday. Which of the three tests would still catch the Sunday-based week?
hint: Which test compares the range itself?

choices.text: The range tests, on any day
choices.why: Right: `weekOf` returns a different range on every day of the week.

choices.text: All three, because the data changed
choices.why: The total would pass with that data.

choices.text: Only the total test
choices.why: With no Sunday or Monday-after sessions, both versions give the same total.

choices.text: None of them: the bug only shows on Sundays
choices.why: A range comparison shows it on any day.

prompt: How does `WeekScreenTest` find the total?

choices.text: By reading `WeekScreen`'s local variable
choices.why: A Compose test never reads a composable's variables.

choices.text: By its position, the first `Text` on screen
choices.why: Position is fragile; the tag is not.

choices.text: Through a screenshot and text recognition
choices.why: The semantics tree holds the text already.

choices.text: By its test tag
choices.why: Right: `onNodeWithTag("total")`.

prompt: Why does the test find the checkbox with `onChildren().filter(isToggleable())` rather than by its text?

choices.text: A checkbox carries no text
choices.why: Right: the toggleable child is the one to act on.

choices.text: Text finders are deprecated in this BOM
choices.why: They are not; the test uses one for the total.

choices.text: Robolectric cannot click a node found by text
choices.why: Section 04 of lesson 20 clicked buttons by text.

choices.text: To make the test run faster
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

prompt: After the Wednesday session was ticked, how many minutes did the total say were done?
The deprecation warning says the `v2` rule uses a `StandardTestDispatcher`. What can change in a test that moves to it?

choices.text: Finders stop matching merged nodes
choices.why: Finders are unchanged.

choices.text: Screenshots are taken at a different density
choices.why: The dispatcher has nothing to do with drawing.

choices.text: Coroutines wait in a queue until time advances
choices.why: Right: `waitForIdle()` is one; this lesson's test needed none.

choices.text: Tests must move to `androidTest`
choices.why: The `v2` rule runs on Robolectric too, as section 04 showed.

prompt: To look inside nodes that Compose has merged, a finder takes `useUnmergedTree = ___`.
Which Gradle task saves a new reference picture?

choices.text: `verifyRoborazziDebug`
choices.why: It compares against the saved reference.

choices.text: `recordRoborazziDebug`
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: `testDebugUnitTest`
choices.why: It runs the test without saving or comparing a picture.

choices.text: `connectedDebugAndroidTest`
choices.why: That needs a device and is not about Roborazzi.

prompt: After the padding change, `verifyRoborazziDebug` failed. The new padding is the intended design. What should you do?
hint: A reference re-recorded without looking stops testing.

choices.text: Revert the padding
choices.why: That is for an accident; this change was intended.

choices.text: Delete the screenshot test
choices.why: The test was right to ask.

choices.text: Record, look, then commit both
choices.why: Right: the reviewer then sees the picture move.

choices.text: Raise the comparison threshold until it passes
choices.why: That hides this change and the next accidental one.

prompt: Why must the reference PNG go into version control?
hint: It is a claim about the screen.

choices.text: It is needed by the app at run time
choices.why: It never ships in the app.

choices.text: Play Console asks for screenshots from tests
choices.why: Store screenshots are a separate thing.

choices.text: Gradle refuses to run without it
choices.why: Without one, a verify run simply has nothing to compare.

choices.text: Its changes appear in review
choices.why: Right: a reviewer can look at the image that moved.

prompt: A library update changes Material's button corner radius. What happens to a project with forty screenshot tests, each showing a button?

choices.text: Only the first test fails
choices.why: Each compares on its own.

choices.text: All forty fail at once, and each must be looked at
choices.why: Right: which is why one screenshot per screen and state is enough.

choices.text: The build refuses the update
choices.why: The build accepts it; the tests report it.

choices.text: Nothing; screenshots ignore library changes
choices.why: Everything that draws is in the picture.

choices.text: `No connected devices!`

prompt: Which two additions did the build file need before an instrumented test could be built?

choices.text: The emulator package
choices.why: That is for running, not building, and lives in the SDK.

choices.text: A runner and a test library

choices.text: Robolectric for `androidTest`
choices.why: On a device the framework is real; Robolectric has no role.

choices.text: A signing key and `minSdk` 33

choices.text: That `offerFor` returns `Explain`

prompt: Why does section 07 advise against a test that counts how often a function inside the screen was called?

choices.text: It tests the wiring, not the result
choices.why: Right: it tests the implementation, not the behaviour.

choices.why: It is possible; it is the wrong thing to check.

choices.text: It runs too slowly on Robolectric
choices.why: Speed is not the objection.

choices.text: Google forbids it in the test libraries
choices.why: Nothing forbids it.

prompt: A test passes on Robolectric and you have no device. What can you honestly claim?

choices.text: It holds on the stand-in Android, not yet on a phone
choices.why: Right: close and deterministic, and not a phone.

choices.text: Nothing, until an instrumented test passes
choices.why: A Robolectric pass is real evidence, with a known limit.

choices.text: That the release build is correct
choices.why: The tests ran against the debug variant.

choices.text: That the app works on every phone
